s1.syndrome_frame: Pruritic rash with erythematous annular plaques and perivascular inflammation
salient_findings: Erythematous annular plaques without scale on the arms and legs
Superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils on biopsy
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 70s
Patient has recurrent primary peritoneal carcinoma
Patient is receiving pembrolizumab and ipilimumab
Rash started as an erythematous papule on the right arm 2 months after initiation of immunotherapy
Rash gradually enlarged and spread to involve both legs
Patient denied any new systemic symptoms associated with onset of the rash
Oral terbinafine trial yielded no improvement
Biopsy showed superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils
PAS stain was negative for fungal organisms

raw.rationale: The patient's rash started 2 months after initiation of pembrolizumab and ipilimumab, suggesting an immune-related adverse event, and the biopsy findings of superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils are consistent with an immune-mediated reaction.

rejected.label: Erythema annulare centrifugum
rejected.why: While the rash has an annular appearance, the temporal association with immunotherapy initiation and the biopsy findings suggest a drug-induced cause rather than a primary dermatological condition.

rejected.label: Ipilimumab-induced rash
rejected.why: Although ipilimumab can cause rashes, pembrolizumab is more commonly associated with cutaneous immune-related adverse events, making it a more likely culprit in this case.

rejected.label: Eosinophilic cellulitis
rejected.why: The presence of eosinophils on biopsy is consistent with this diagnosis, but the clinical presentation and temporal association with immunotherapy initiation make pembrolizumab-induced rash a more likely explanation.

rejected.label: Urticaria
rejected.why: The rash does not have the characteristic wheals and hives of urticaria, and the biopsy findings do not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Fixed drug eruption
rejected.why: The rash does not have the typical targetoid appearance of fixed drug eruption, and the biopsy findings do not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Erythema multiforme
rejected.why: The rash does not have the characteristic target lesions of erythema multiforme, and the biopsy findings do not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Granuloma annulare
rejected.why: The biopsy findings do not show the characteristic granulomatous inflammation of granuloma annulare, making this diagnosis unlikely.
